**Best all-around pick: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic + 220W panel — about $699.** It pairs a 1,024Wh LiFePO₄ battery with 1,800W of AC output, and the cited deal includes a 220W bifacial panel. That’s a good balance for camping and basic outage backup. [See the deal details](https://www.techradar.com/pro/ecoflows-delta-3-solar-generator-bundle-gets-a-usd300-price-drop-at-amazon-with-the-portable-power-station-and-220w-solar-panel-built-for-camping-home-backup-and-emergencies).  

**Best value if you want more panel: ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 400W kit — about $731.** It also has a 1,024Wh LiFePO₄ battery, but includes 400W of panels—twice the panel wattage of many similarly sized kits. [Check the kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit); the listed price uses code **ALLPOWERS26**.

For a simpler brand-name alternative, the **Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2** is listed around $699 with a 200W panel and 1,070Wh capacity. Whichever you choose, prices can change, and real-world solar output is typically below the panel’s rated wattage. [Compare the kits and specs](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included).
